description: Tidal Marsh and Dune Restoration on Prime Hook National Wildlife Refuge is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USFWS, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. With the increase in storm frequency and sea level rise, refuge staff decided to transition the impoundments to a salt marsh system to be more resilient to climate change. Coverage: Prime Hook National Wildlife Refuge (2024). The toolkit gives Prime Hook National Wildlife Refuge as the location, 2024 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
